figures.caption: Fig. 3 Questions that require an attribute not stored in the table (n = 1,500). a, Derivedvalue F1 for FD-SCoPE and four alternatives using the same language model. b, Share of questions for which every row of the answer was correct. c, Share of questions for which exactly the reference set of trial records was returned. d, Sensitivity and positive predictive value for retrieving the relevant trial records. e, Flow of the 1,500 questions through FD-SCoPE: the value was computed by a verified program reused from an earlier question, derived row by row by the model, or computed by a newly induced and verified program, or no trial matched the question; band width is proportional to the number of questions, and blue bands lead to answers that were correct in every row. Bars in a–d are bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Values are in Supplementary Tables S3 and S4.

Fig. 4 Effect of corrections on held-out questions. Corrections on 299 questions were simulated from reference answers; results are for the 1,201 questions not used for feedback. a, Question-level measures before and after feedback. b, Accuracy of individual derived values for all trials, and for trials excluded from learning when corrections were drawn from half of the trials. Numbers beside the points are the change in percentage points. Values are in Supplementary Table S5.

Fig. 1 FD-SCoPE architecture. Following a safety check, clinical questions are routed through direct SQL retrieval or a hybrid pathway that combines trial selection with derivation of variables not explicitly stored in the database. Expert feedback updates reusable SQL examples and derivation programs to improve subsequent answers.

Fig. 5 Derived-value F1 by derivation family and approach. Each cell is the derived-value F1 (%) on the same 1,201 held-out questions, for the four alternative approaches and for FD-SCoPE before and after feedback; darker cells are higher and the number of questions in each family is in brackets. Families are ordered by the change that feedback produced. Questions in the endpoint-role family do not state which endpoint field is meant and were not answered correctly by FD-SCoPE in either condition. Values are in Supplementary Table S6.
Table 1 Question sets used in the evaluation.

Fig. 6 Component analysis and robustness to phrasing. a,b, Derived-attribute questions (304-question subset): derived-value F1 and share of questions with every row correct for the full system and with one component removed or replaced. c, Recorded-field questions (300 held-out benchmark questions): exact-match accuracy with one component removed. d, Exact-match accuracy as a function of the share of the approved-example bank that is available; the band is the bootstrap 95% confidence interval. e,f, Exact-match accuracy and execution F1 on original and reworded questions with the reference answer unchanged; numbers in brackets are question counts and numbers beside the points are the change in percentage points. Bars in a–c are bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Values are in Supplementary Tables S7, S8, S10 and S11.

Fig. 2 Clinician-style tasks and benchmark questions about recorded fields. a, Share of 140 clinician-style tasks answered correctly by FD-SCoPE and seven alternatives using the same language model; few-shot, zero-shot and chain-of-thought are the prompting baselines. b, The same result by task type, with the number of tasks in brackets; each grey dot is one alternative, and ‘Control’ denotes listings of trials with a comparator other than chemotherapy. c, Exact-match accuracy on the 1,500 benchmark questions. d, Execution F1 on the same questions. e, Exact-match accuracy with two language models. Bars are 95% confidence intervals (Wilson in a, bootstrap in c–e). Values are in Supplementary Tables S1 and S9.
